prerequisites: Basic mathematical knowledge, as taught in the basic modules Fundamentals of Linear Algebra and Fundamentals of Analysis, is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can work with regular expressions, finite automata, and grammars.
Students know their possibilities and limitations.
Students understand formal models of computation.
Students know the fundamental limits of algorithmic computation.
Students know the limits of efficiently solving problems.
Students can follow scientific working methods (identifying, formulating, solving problems, training abstract thinking).
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Automata theory and formal languages: Grammars and Chomsky Hierarchy
Computability: Various models of computability: Turing, Loop, and While computability

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercises

assessment_rules: To acquire credits, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercises and orally present the solution to at least two of the exercises. Grading is based on the written exam, from 0 to 15 points, according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Computer Science program.
